title: Adaptive DHiSparse: Speculative Decoding over a Load-Adaptive KV Hierarchy
summary: The method replaces fixed-budget hierarchical sparse KV serving (HiSparse) and non-speculative adaptive serving by combining host-memory KV offloading with exact fused retrieval, speculative decoding (DSpark/DFlash2), and residency that expands or contracts with load. It costs engineering complexity: shared missing-row retrieval across queries, a window-bounded draft KV ring, verification staging reused across layer groups, and a load-adaptive residency controller, plus host-memory capacity and PCIe transfer bandwidth. It can fail at low concurrency or short contexts where offload and retrieval overhead dominate, when host-GPU bandwidth is saturated, or if the exact retrieval path and speculative acceptance interact poorly with draft-model quality, eroding the acceptance-rate assumptions behind the throughput claims.
rationale: The reported gains require 100K-500K contexts, concurrency of 128-512, and multi-GPU decode serving with specific draft frameworks, none of which fit a single 24 GB GPU or API-based production setup, so the technique is worth tracking rather than adopting or testing now.
technique: Load-adaptive hierarchical KV with speculative decoding

claims.statement: The method replaces fixed-budget hierarchical sparse KV serving (HiSparse) and non-speculative adaptive serving by combining host-memory KV offloading with exact fused retrieval, speculative decoding (DSpark/DFlash2), and residency that expands or contracts with load. It costs engineering complexity: shared missing-row retrieval across queries, a window-bounded draft KV ring, verification staging reused across layer groups, and a load-adaptive residency controller, plus host-memory capacity and PCIe transfer bandwidth. It can fail at low concurrency or short contexts where offload and retrieval overhead dominate, when host-GPU bandwidth is saturated, or if the exact retrieval path and speculative acceptance interact poorly with draft-model quality, eroding the acceptance-rate assumptions behind the throughput claims.

At 500K context and concurrency 512 on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Adaptive DHiSparse with DSpark delivers 1.85x the output tokens of resident serving with DSpark; at 100K context and concurrency 128 on GLM-5.3 with DFlash2 it reaches 793 output tokens/s per decode GPU, 1.45x HiSparse, and sustains up to 4x the concurrency under equal latency bounds.
